CUSTOM EQUALIZER - ON:
a) Enable the Custom Equalizer toggle.
b) Adjust individual frequency bands:
   - Bass (low frequencies): 60Hz, 150Hz
   - Midrange: 400Hz, 1kHz, 2.4kHz
   - Treble (high frequencies): 6kHz, 15kHz
c) Play audio content (music with varied frequencies recommended).
d) Verify each frequency adjustment affects audio output appropriately.
e) Test extreme settings (max boost/cut) for distortion.
f) Create and save a custom EQ preset.

CUSTOM EQUALIZER - OFF:
a) Disable the Custom Equalizer toggle.
b) Play the same audio content.
c) Verify audio returns to flat/default response.
5) Reboot the machine and relaunch the Dolby app.
6) Verify EQ settings are retained through reboot.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria: Expected Result: Graphic Equalizer is adjustable and savable. Settings are retained through reboot. Audio enhancement is clearly detectable without glitching, popping, or audio drops.

   a) Ensure LE Audio headphones/earbuds is paired with the device.
   b) Verify device supports LE Audio profile (not just Classic Bluetooth).
   c) Turn on LE Audio device and verify it's in range.
   d) Confirm device is NOT currently connected.
2) Open Media Player app:
   a) Click Start → search "Media Player" → launch app.
   b) Select audio or video file and start playback.
   c) Verify audio is playing through DUT speakers.
3) Connect LE Audio device during playback:
   a) While audio is playing, connect LE Audio device:
      - Click Bluetooth icon in system tray → select LE Audio device, OR
      - Go to Settings → Bluetooth & devices → click on paired device.
   b) Wait for LE Audio connection to establish.
   c) Observe system behavior and audio routing.
4) Verify audio transition:
   a) Confirm audio switches from DUT speakers to LE Audio device.
   b) Check if transition is automatic after connection.
   c) Verify minimal audio interruption during switch.
   d) Confirm playback continues after transition.
5) Verify LE Audio quality after transition:
   a) Listen for high-quality audio through LE Audio device.
   b) Verify lower latency compared to Classic Bluetooth.
   c) Check audio/video sync (for video content).
   d) Confirm LC3 codec provides clear audio.
   e) Verify no dropouts or connection issues.
6) Verify system audio settings:
   a) Right-click speaker icon → Sound settings.
   b) Confirm LE Audio device shows as active output.
   c) Verify LE Audio profile is active (check device properties).
testScenarios.passFailCriteria: Expected Result: Audio transitions from DUT speakers to LE Audio device when connected during Media Player playback. LE Audio provides low-latency, high-quality audio. Playback continues seamlessly.

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1) Open Media Player app:
   a) Click Start → search "Media Player" → launch app.
   b) Select audio or video file for playback.
   c) Set audio output to DUT speakers at 50% volume.
2) Start content playback:
   a) Begin playing audio or video content.
   b) Verify audio is playing clearly.
   c) Note the current playback position/timestamp.
3) Initiate Sleep mode:
   a) While audio/video is playing, put device to sleep:
      - Press Power button briefly, OR
      - Click Start → Power → Sleep, OR
      - Press Win+X → Shut down or sign out → Sleep.
   b) Verify device enters sleep mode (screen off, indicators dim).
4) Verify sleep behavior:
   a) Confirm audio stops when device enters sleep.
   b) Verify no audio continues playing during sleep.
   c) Wait 30 seconds to 1 minute in sleep mode.
5) Wake device from sleep:
   a) Press Power button or any key to wake device.
   b) Sign in if prompted (PIN/password/Windows Hello).
   c) Verify device resumes to desktop.
6) Verify Media Player state after wake:
   a) Check if Media Player app is still open.
   b) Verify playback state (paused or stopped).
   c) Note the playback position - should be near where sleep occurred.
   d) Click Play to resume playback.
7) Verify audio quality after resume:
   a) Listen for clear audio without distortion.
   b) Verify correct audio endpoint is still selected.
   c) Check volume level is preserved.
   d) Confirm no audio glitches or artifacts.
   e) Verify audio/video sync (for video content).
8) Test extended playback after wake:
   a) Continue playback for 2-3 minutes.
   b) Verify stable audio without dropouts.
   c) Test playback controls (pause, seek, volume).
testScenarios.passFailCriteria: Expected Result: Device enters sleep correctly, stopping audio playback. After wake, Media Player resumes properly. Audio quality is maintained. Playback can be resumed without issues.

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1) Prepare channel test files:
   a) Obtain audio sweep test files (left channel only, right channel only, stereo both).
   b) Copy test files to local storage accessible by Media Player.
   c) Verify files are standard format (WAV or MP3 recommended).
2) Configure audio output:
   a) Set Output device to DUT speakers or headphones (stereo capable).
   b) Set volume to 50% baseline.
   c) Verify stereo output is enabled (not mono).
3) Test Left Channel Sweep:
   a) Open Media Player and load left-channel-only sweep file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify audio plays ONLY from left speaker/ear.
   d) Listen for full frequency sweep (20Hz to 20kHz range).
   e) Confirm no audio bleeds to right channel.
   f) Note any dropouts or distortion.
4) Test Right Channel Sweep:
   a) Load right-channel-only sweep file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify audio plays ONLY from right speaker/ear.
   d) Listen for full frequency sweep.
   e) Confirm no audio bleeds to left channel.
   f) Note any dropouts or distortion.
5) Test Both Channels (Stereo) Sweep:
   a) Load stereo sweep file with both channels.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify audio plays equally from both speakers/ears.
   d) Check stereo balance is even (no channel louder than other).
   e) Listen for full frequency range coverage.
6) Test channel separation at different volumes:
   a) Repeat left/right tests at 25%, 75%, 100% volume.
   b) Verify channel isolation maintained at all levels.
   c) Check for any crosstalk at high volumes.
7) Test with headphones (if not already):
   a) Connect 3.5mm or USB headphones.
   b) Repeat left, right, and stereo sweep tests.
   c) Verify proper channel assignment (L=Left ear, R=Right ear).
testScenarios.passFailCriteria: Expected Result: Media Player correctly routes left-only audio to left channel, right-only to right channel, and stereo to both channels evenly. No crosstalk or channel bleeding. Full frequency range reproduced.

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1) Prepare sample rate test files:
   a) Obtain audio files at 44.1kHz, 48kHz, and 96kHz sample rates.
   b) Use same audio content at different sample rates for comparison.
   c) Prefer WAV or FLAC format to avoid codec variables.
   d) Copy test files to local storage.
2) Configure audio output:
   a) Set Output device to DUT speakers or high-quality headphones.
   b) Set volume to 50% baseline.
   c) Verify audio device supports all test sample rates.
3) Test 44.1kHz playback:
   a) Open Media Player and load 44.1kHz audio file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify audio plays without errors or glitches.
   d) Listen for clear audio quality (CD-quality standard).
   e) Check for any pitch issues or playback speed problems.
   f) Verify no dropouts during continuous playback.
4) Test 48kHz playback:
   a) Load 48kHz audio file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify smooth playback without sample rate conversion issues.
   d) Listen for clear audio quality (DVD/video standard).
   e) Compare quality to 44.1kHz if audibly different.
   f) Verify no clicks, pops, or artifacts.
5) Test 96kHz playback:
   a) Load 96kHz high-resolution audio file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify Media Player handles high sample rate.
   d) Listen for high-resolution audio quality.
   e) Check for any buffer underruns or glitches.
   f) Note if system resamples to lower rate (check Sound settings).
6) Test sample rate switching:
   a) Play 44.1kHz file, then immediately switch to 48kHz file.
   b) Verify smooth transition without audio glitches.
   c) Switch to 96kHz file.
   d) Verify no errors during rate transitions.
7) Test extended playback at each rate:
   a) Play each sample rate file for 2+ minutes continuously.
   b) Verify stable playback without degradation.
   c) Check CPU usage remains reasonable.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria: Expected Result: Media Player correctly plays audio files at 44.1kHz, 48kHz, and 96kHz sample rates. No playback errors, pitch issues, or quality degradation. Smooth transitions between different sample rates.

testCases.testName: MP4, MOV, AVI, WMV, M4V, M2V

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1) Prepare video format test files:
   a) Obtain video files in each format: MP4, MOV, AVI, WMV, M4V, M2V.
   b) Ensure each video has clear audio track for testing.
   c) Use videos with dialogue and music for quality assessment.
   d) Copy all test files to local storage.
2) Configure audio output:
   a) Set Output device to DUT speakers or headphones.
   b) Set volume to 50% baseline.
   c) Verify audio output is working.
3) Test MP4 format:
   a) Open Media Player and load MP4 video file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify video plays with audio.
   d) Check audio-video synchronization (lip sync).
   e) Listen for clear audio quality.
   f) Test seek functionality - verify audio resyncs.
   g) Note any codec compatibility issues.
4) Test MOV format:
   a) Load MOV (QuickTime) video file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify audio plays correctly.
   d) Check A/V sync throughout playback.
   e) Test pause/resume - verify audio continuity.
5) Test AVI format:
   a) Load AVI video file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify audio codec support (various AVI audio codecs).
   d) Check for audio delay or sync issues.
   e) Test playback controls.
6) Test WMV format:
   a) Load WMV (Windows Media Video) file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify native Windows format plays smoothly.
   d) Check audio quality (typically WMA audio track).
   e) Verify seeking works correctly.
7) Test M4V format:
   a) Load M4V (iTunes video) file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify audio decodes correctly.
   d) Check for any DRM-related playback issues.
   e) Test playback stability.
8) Test M2V format:
   a) Load M2V (MPEG-2 video) file.
   b) Start playback (may require separate audio file).
   c) Verify video codec support.
   d) Check audio track handling.
9) Extended playback test:
   a) Play each format for 3+ minutes.
   b) Verify no audio dropouts or sync drift.
   c) Check for memory or performance issues.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria: Expected Result: Media Player correctly plays audio from all video formats (MP4, MOV, AVI, WMV, M4V, M2V). Audio remains synchronized with video. No codec errors or playback failures.

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1) Prepare audio format test files:
   a) Obtain audio files in each format: WMA, MP3, AAC, FLAC, WAV.
   b) Use same or similar audio content across formats for comparison.
   c) Include files with various bitrates where applicable.
   d) Copy all test files to local storage.
2) Configure audio output:
   a) Set Output device to DUT speakers or high-quality headphones.
   b) Set volume to 50% baseline.
   c) Verify audio output is working.
3) Test WMA format:
   a) Open Media Player and load WMA file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify native Windows Media Audio format plays correctly.
   d) Listen for audio quality - check for compression artifacts.
   e) Test at different WMA bitrates if available (64, 128, 192 kbps).
   f) Verify metadata/tags display correctly.
4) Test MP3 format:
   a) Load MP3 file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify universal MP3 format plays without issues.
   d) Test different bitrates (128, 192, 256, 320 kbps).
   e) Check for any decoding artifacts.
   f) Verify ID3 tag display.
5) Test AAC format:
   a) Load AAC/M4A file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify Advanced Audio Coding format plays correctly.
   d) Compare quality to MP3 at similar bitrate.
   e) Check for any compatibility issues.
   f) Verify metadata displays.
6) Test FLAC format:
   a) Load FLAC lossless audio file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify lossless audio quality.
   d) Listen for full dynamic range and clarity.
   e) Check CPU usage (FLAC decoding requirements).
   f) Test high-resolution FLAC if available (24-bit/96kHz).
7) Test WAV format:
   a) Load WAV uncompressed audio file.
   b) Start playback.
   c) Verify uncompressed PCM audio plays perfectly.
   d) Check for any latency or buffer issues.
   e) Test different WAV specifications (16-bit, 24-bit).
8) Test format switching:
   a) Create playlist with all formats mixed.
   b) Play through playlist - verify smooth transitions.
   c) Check for gaps or glitches between formats.
9) Test playback controls per format:
   a) For each format, test pause/play, seek, and volume.
   b) Verify all controls work consistently across formats.
   c) Check progress bar accuracy for each format.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria: Expected Result: Media Player correctly plays all audio formats (WMA, MP3, AAC, FLAC, WAV). Each format decoded properly with appropriate quality. Seamless transitions between formats. All playback controls function correctly.

2) Configure audio output for DUT:
